blocks.text: SAN FERNANDO CITY, La Union — The La Union provincial government is distributing drought-resilient crop seeds and farm inputs, installing solar-powered irrigation systems, rehabilitating water impounding structures and expanding rainwater harvesting facilities as it prepares for the anticipated effects of a Super El Niño. These interventions aim to sustain agricultural production, protect farmers’ livelihoods and ensure water availability during prolonged dry conditions from November 2026 to March 2027. La Union Gov. Mario Eduardo C. Ortega has directed various departments to help farmers cope with prolonged dry conditions and protect communities that may face water shortages and heat-related illnesses.
